this paper presents a novel box level supervised learning based multispectral pedestrian detection approach that is capable of obtaining more accurate detection results than the existing state of the art anchor box based approaches and is more computationally efficient.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our proposed method achieves 1.2% and 2.2% improvements over the best performing anchor based multispectral pedestrian detection method in terms of AP50 and AP75, respectively.

The main takeaway from our work is that
accurate pedestrian detection is achievable using small size input image patches and our proposed method can be easily integrated with existing real time detection frameworks.
the box level segmentation based framework is more suitable for multispectral pedestrian detection than the anchor box based one.
accurate pedestrian detection can be achieved by fusing multispectral information in the box level segmentation supervised deep neural network, without the need of hyperparameter tuning.
